samples.summary: Workflow change is shipped as an inert `.patch` file plus instructions for a privileged human to `git apply` it, routing around the GitHub App's deliberately-withheld `workflows` permission with no integrity binding
samples.evidence: The `workflows` scope is withheld from the `yorkie-agent[bot]` installation precisely so agent-authored code cannot modify CI/CD — the workflows that hold `secrets.AGENT_APP_ID`/`AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` (.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1481-1482) and the promotion/merge gates themselves. This change carries the workflow edit as data (`docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-workflow.patch`) and the todo instructs a maintainer or 'a credential with Workflows: write' to run `git apply <patch>` (todo.md:76-81). Attack path: any agent-authored branch can place arbitrary text in a `docs/**/*.patch` file; nothing in the pipeline validates such a file (knip, eslint, tsc and the docs backtick-path check all ignore `.patch` content, and `scripts/test/agent-workflow-guards.test.mjs` only inspects real `.github/workflows/*.yml`). Once the ritual is normalized, a patch that adds `pull_request_target:`, a step that echoes `${{ secrets.AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}`, or that deletes the ready-gate entirely lands with a single hand-applied command, and the applied bytes are never re-checked against the bytes CI reviewed — the maintainer applies whatever is at HEAD at apply time, which may not be what the reviewer read. The specific patch here is benign (it only rewrites the promote step's exit-code handling and adds no permissions or secrets), so the finding is about the channel, not this payload. Mitigation: a maintainer applying such a patch must review it as privileged workflow code, and the repo should gate `.patch` files that touch `.github/workflows/**` (e.g. a CI check that fails unless the patch is accompanied by an explicit approval marker / hash).

samples.summary: Gate 1 ('unforgeable' CI evidence) identifies the CI run by its mutable display name `r.name === "CI"` rather than by workflow id/path; the new test pins the weak identifier
samples.evidence: `ciPassed` reads every workflow run for the head SHA and keeps only those whose *display name* is the string "CI" (mark-ready.mjs:133), then trusts the newest one's conclusion (:136-137). The header calls this evidence 'the author agent cannot create or forge a CI run' (:5-10), but the `name` field is just the `name:` key of whatever workflow file produced the run — for `pull_request` events that file comes from the PR head. Anyone who can add `.github/workflows/anything.yml` containing `name: CI` and a job that exits 0 produces a run named "CI", `conclusion: success`, for the head SHA; because the newest run wins the sort it overrides the real red CI run, satisfying the one gate that means 'the tests passed' and letting the PR be flipped to ready. The only thing standing in the way is the very `workflows`-permission boundary that this change's `.patch`-file hand-apply ritual is designed to work around, and a `agent:managed` human-authored PR (agent-iterate-ci.yml:38-47) is not blocked by it at all. The new test at scripts/agent/mark-ready.test.mjs:184-209 locks in the name-based match instead of a `path === ".github/workflows/ci.yml"` / `workflow_id` match. Confidence is low because I could not confirm on this repo that a head-branch-added workflow's run is returned by `actions/runs?head_sha=` with the attacker-chosen name before the real CI run concludes.

samples.summary: The branch deliberately ships a red assertion that pins a promotion-gate control, and documents it as acceptable — exposing that control to the automated CI-fixer whose only available 'fix' is to weaken it
samples.evidence: todo.md:83-86 states the `agent-review-panel.yml handles every mark-ready code, defaults the rest` test 'fails on purpose' because the consumer half cannot be pushed. That test (scripts/agent/mark-ready.test.mjs:329-399) is the only thing pinning the shape of the ready-gate consumer: that it passes `--promote`, that it captures the real exit status, that an unenumerated status fails the job, and that the succeed-quietly branch is corroborated. A red CI on an `agent/` branch triggers `agent-iterate-ci.yml` (workflow_run on CI/completed, conclusion failure, branch `agent/*` — lines 19-47), which feeds the failure to an agent with `contents: write` and asks it to fix and push. That agent cannot push `.github/workflows/**`, so the only edit that makes the suite green is deleting, skipping or weakening the security-relevant assertions in `mark-ready.test.mjs` — and the doc in-repo pre-declares the red state legitimate, which is exactly the text an automated fixer or a hurried reviewer would use to justify neutering the assertion. Impact if it happens: the promote job's exit-code/`--promote` contract becomes unpinned again. Confidence low: the fixer is also `vars.AGENT_PIPELINE_ENABLED`-gated and may simply exhaust MAX_ATTEMPTS=4 and page instead.

samples.summary: The test's `gh` stub writes the value of `GH_TOKEN` in cleartext to a temp file that is never cleaned up, so any call site that forgets to override the credential leaks a real token to disk
samples.evidence: The stub appends `process.env.GH_TOKEN` verbatim to `$GH_STUB_TOKEN_LOG` on every invocation (mark-ready.test.mjs:51-54), and `run()` spawns the CLI with the full ambient environment spread in (`...process.env`, :114) before overriding `GH_TOKEN`/`GH_MUTATION_TOKEN` with stub values (:119-120). Today every path goes through `run()`, so only `stub-app-token`/`stub-default-token` are written — but the harness is one copied helper or one removed override away from writing a live GitHub App installation token into `mkdtempSync(tmpdir(), "mark-ready-")` (:103), which nothing in the file ever deletes; the files persist for the life of the machine/runner and would be picked up by any `/tmp` artifact upload or developer-machine backup. Prefer logging a non-secret discriminator (e.g. `token === process.env.GH_MUTATION_TOKEN ? "mutation" : "read"`) computed inside the stub rather than the credential itself, and remove the temp dir after each run.

samples.summary: The promote step now merges stderr into a log file that is `cat`ed to the step log and left in `$RUNNER_TEMP` for the rest of the job
samples.evidence: The patch redirects `2>&1` into `$RUNNER_TEMP/mark-ready.log` and unconditionally `cat`s it (patch lines 15 and 24). mark-ready's failure paths interpolate `execFileSync` error text — which carries the failing `gh` argv and gh's stderr, i.e. API response bodies — into stdout/stderr (scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:111, 208-212, 237, 263), and those calls are made with the App installation token. Actions masks the registered `steps.app-token.outputs.token` and `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`, so this is hardening rather than a leak, but the log also now persists in `$RUNNER_TEMP` for every later step of the promote job (including third-party `actions/download-artifact` steps at agent-review-panel.yml:1537-1543) instead of being write-once to the step log as before. Deleting the log after the `case`, or redirecting only stdout, keeps the blast radius where it was.

verdict.reason: The artifacts exist as described, but the finding is a process-hardening suggestion rather than a blocking security weakness. The patch (docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-workflow.patch:1-51) is inert text: a Grep for `git apply|git am|patch -p|\.patch` across .github/ returns no matches, so nothing in CI or any workflow applies docs/**/*.patch. The only application path is a human/credential that already holds `Workflows: write` (todo.md:76-81) — the same trust anchor GitHub's withheld `workflows` scope preserves — so the channel confers no capability the agent otherwise lacks and no escalation over what that credential can already do by hand; the exploit chain requires a privileged human to commit workflow bytes they chose not to read, identical to merging any workflow-touching PR. The shipped payload contains no `permissions:`, no trigger change, and no `secrets.*` reference (verified line by line). Once applied, the bytes become ordinary workflow content that scripts/test/agent-workflow-guards.test.mjs:39-80 enumerates from disk and asserts invariants over, plus the mark-ready.test.mjs cross-file contract. There is no missing or weakened gate on an enforced path, no secret exposure, and no injection — the requested mitigation (a CI check gating .patch files with an approval marker/hash) is defense-in-depth, i.e. minor/nit under this lens's severity rubric, not major/blocking.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as claimed: mark-ready.mjs:133 selects the CI evidence with `r.name === "CI"` (mutable display name) and :136-137 trusts the newest such run's conclusion, while the header at :4-10 bills this as unforgeable, separate-actor evidence. The repo's own sibling call sites identify the same workflow by immutable id (agent-loop.yml:143, agent-rerun.yml:187, agent-iterate-ci.yml:163 all use `workflow_id: 'ci.yml'`), so mark-ready is the outlier; ci.yml:4 confirms `name: CI` is just a file key any workflow file can claim. The gate is on the enforced path (agent-review-panel.yml:1444-1496 runs `mark-ready.mjs "$PR" --promote`). The new test at mark-ready.test.mjs:184-209 does pin the name-based match rather than a workflow_id/path match. I considered `already-guarded`: the GitHub App lacks the `workflows` permission (docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-todo.md:61-74 shows the server-side push rejection), which blocks the autonomous agent from adding a workflow file — but the repository itself documents that this barrier is not universal: agent-review-panel.yml:51 states "The agent App cannot push `.github/workflows/**`, but an `agent:managed` human PR can." So an agent:managed head branch can introduce a workflow named CI whose green run, being newest, overrides the real red CI run. That is a partial mitigation, not an unreachability guard. The issue is authorization/evidence-integrity (forgeable gate evidence), squarely in the security lane; impact is bounded by the fact that promotion only flips draft→ready and never merges (mark-ready.mjs:22-25), which matches the reviewer's major severity rather than justifying a drop.

verdict.reason: Every factual claim checks out: docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-todo.md:83-86 does pre-declare the red test legitimate; scripts/agent/mark-ready.test.mjs:329-399 does pin --promote, code=$?, the non-pipe redirect and the *) default; .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1494-1504 still carries the old bare `if [ "$code" -eq N ]` chain with no log redirect, so that test genuinely fails today; and .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:19-25,44-47,67 does dispatch a contents:write fixer on failed CI for agent/* branches. The finding is therefore REAL as described but is not blocking under the Security rubric. The artifact at risk is a node --test assertion file, not an enforced runtime gate: the promote job's behavior is untouched and still emits ready=true only for code 0 (agent-review-panel.yml:1504), so nothing is presently promoted that should not be, and the immediate effect of the red assertion is a RED merge gate, which is fail-safe rather than permissive. There is no attacker in the chain and no authorization bypass, secret exposure, injection, or broken cryptographic check; the harm requires a hypothetical future automated agent to delete a test, and the stated impact ("the contract becomes unpinned again") is loss of regression coverage — the rubric explicitly lists test quality and process/design fit as out of this lens's lane. The dispatch path is additionally bounded by vars.AGENT_PIPELINE_ENABLED (agent-iterate-ci.yml:45), the unforgeable MAX_ATTEMPTS=4 failed-CI counter that pages a human (agent-iterate-ci.yml:35,208-222), and a fixer prompt that directs root-cause repair and staying in scope (agent-iterate-ci.yml:383-390), with any edit landing as a reviewable commit. This belongs to the correctness/process reviewer, not the security merge gate.
